articles.title: ‘I feel I have won the Olympic gold once again’: MM Somaya gets medal back as Bengaluru Police crack theft case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India hockey captain MM Somaya has got back his prized 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal after Bengaluru Police cracked the theft case and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India hockey captain MM Somaya has got back his prized 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal after Bengaluru Police cracked the theft case and recovered the stolen medals and other valuables from his residence. Two people have been arrested in connection with the incident, bringing relief to the three-time Olympian, who described the recovery as an emotional moment.Expressing gratitude to the police for their efforts, Somaya said their reassurance throughout the investigation had helped him remain hopeful that the medals would be recovered."I am extremely grateful to the Bangalore Police, headed by Mr Seemant (Kumar Singh), who have worked really hard over the last few days. They have not been able to recover only the medal, but also some valuables stolen from my residence," Somaya told reporters.He also acknowledged the efforts of DCP East Dr Vikram, the ACP of Halsur, police inspector Anand and the Indiranagar police team, who had assured him from the beginning that the medals would be traced."They are an honor not only for me personally but it is an honor for the state and the country. So he was very reassuring and he and his team at the Indiranagar Police station have done a magnificent job. And I'm really grateful to them. I feel I have won the Olympic medal once again. I am really happy with how police handled this case and cracked within a short period," he added.Two arrested, all stolen medals and valuables recoveredBengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said the police had recovered all the stolen medals and valuables and handed them back to Somaya after completing the legal formalities."This case of the theft which was reported in Indira Nagar police station by Mr Somaiya about the theft of gold medal and silver medals which he had won so in such a great manner for the pride of the country. So today we are happy that my entire team could detect that case, two people have been arrested and all the valuables as well as all the medals which were stolen have been recovered and we deem it our privilege to have handed over all the medals to Mr Somaiya as per legal formalities after being completed," he told ANI.Singh described the investigation as one of the most challenging cases for the police because there were no initial clues. He said the two arrested accused had been involved in similar crimes earlier and that the police would ensure they did not repeat such offences."This is reassuring for us, motivating for us, especially for our lower forces who keep working day and night and this was one of the most challenging cases for us because we didn't have any clue for it. So finally we could detect this case and recover the items and those two people who are there, they are the accused who have been caught are people who have been involved in such crimes earlier also. We will see to it that in future they do not do such an act," he added.Somaya recalls shock of theft, emotional value of Olympic goldThe theft took place on October 28, when Somaya and his family were away on a short holiday in Coorg, his native place. After being alerted by a neighbour, they rushed back to Bengaluru and registered a complaint, with an FIR filed on the same day."Actually we had gone to Coorg (at the time of theft), my native place, for a short holiday and this happened by the thieves breaking into the house which was really a shock for us. Fortunately we were alerted quickly by one of our neighbours and we rushed back from Coorg and were able to register our complaint and also the FIR was filed on the same day," Somaya said.The 1980 Olympic gold holds special significance for Somaya, who also represented India at the 1984 Los Angeles and 1988 Seoul Olympics, captaining the side at the latter. He won silver at the 1982 Asian Games in Delhi and bronze at the 1986 edition in Seoul.Recalling the amateur era of Indian hockey, Somaya explained why the medals meant far more to him than their material value."It (the medals) are many years of work and in those days there was no monetary awards, it was an amateur sport so the medals are a little bit of an honour actually and not only for me but for the state and the country. So I carry a lot of memories and sentiments so it is very special to me, especially the Olympic gold medal and I am really happy that they are back with me now," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Niraj Kumar scripts history with World Championships bronze, secures LA 2028 Olympic quota
articles.summary: India's shooting contingent has received a major boost ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with Niraj Kumar securing an Olympic quota place after
articles.body: India's shooting contingent has received a major boost ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with Niraj Kumar securing an Olympic quota place after winning bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha, Qatar.The 26-year-old delivered a composed performance in the final on Wednesday, finishing third with 346.5 points to claim his maiden individual medal at the World Championships. The achievement also earned India a quota place for the upcoming Summer Games, taking the country's tally at the competition to two.Dmitrii Pimenov, competing as an Individual Neutral Athlete, won the gold medal, while Slovakia's Patrik Jany settled for silver. Norway's Jon-Hermann Hegg finished fourth and secured the third available Olympic quota in the event, as Jany had already earned one for his country.Niraj Kumar ends wait for maiden individual World Championships medalThe bronze medal marks a significant breakthrough for Niraj, who has consistently featured among India's promising rifle shooters. Despite reaching the final of major international competitions on previous occasions, an individual World Championships medal had remained elusive. His performance in Doha finally brought that long-awaited achievement.Niraj also contributed to India's bronze medal in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions team event alongside Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and Akhil Sheoran. The Indian trio finished with a combined score of 1,751 points.Czechia claimed the team gold, while Norway secured silver.India secure second shooting quota for LA 2028 OlympicsNiraj's performance added another Olympic quota to India's shooting tally at the ongoing World Championships. Earlier, Jaypal Malviya had secured India's first quota place after winning silver in the men's 10m air pistol event.The qualification places India in a stronger position as the shooting contingent begins its preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. However, the quota place is allocated to India and does not guarantee Niraj an automatic selection for the Games. The final decision on the participating shooter will be taken by the Indian shooting authorities closer to the Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: María Pérez entra en el 'Top ten' de mejores atletas del año para World Athletics
articles.standfirst: La granadina fue campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha en Birmingham con un récord mundial
articles.summary: La granadina fue campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha en Birmingham con un récord mundial
articles.body: María Pérez sigue acaparando reconocimientos. La marchadora granadina, oro en el medio maratón marcha del Europeo de Birmingham el pasado verano, ha sido incluida por World Athletics (WA) en su 'top ten' de mejores atletas femeninas de 2026. La atleta de Orce, novena en esta prestigiosa clasificación, se impuso en la ciudad inglesa con un nuevo récord mundial (1h30:06) en una distancia que sustituye a los tradicionales 20 km marcha. Esto le ha valido para sumar un nuevo éxito tras ganar en 2025 el premio como 'Atleta femenina del año' en la categoría de fuera estadio, un galardón que también concede WA. En el Mundial de Tokio, María defendió con éxito su doblete de Budapest 2023 (oros en los 20 y 35 km marcha), convirtiéndose en la primera mujer en reeditar dos títulos mundiales individuales. Las tres nominadas a 'Atleta femenina del año' son la velocidad estadounidense Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, oro en los 100 y 200 metros del Ultimate Championship; su compatriota Masai Russell, nueva plusmarquista mundial de los 100 vallas, y la suiza Audrey Werro, que ha revolucionado el 800 hasta el punto de poner en jaque el vetusto récord mundial de Jarmila Kratochvílová. Cuarta y quinta son la etíope Tigst Assefa y la dominicana Marileidy Paulino. La primera ganó este año los prestigiosos maratones de Londres y Berlín, donde se quedó cerca de asaltar el récord mundial, mientras que la segunda a vuelto a dominar los 400 metros con mano de hierro. Sexta ha sido la keniana Agnes Ngetich, oro mundial tanto en cross como medio maratón, seguida de la lanzadora de peso estadounidense Chase Jackson, campeona mundial indoor y autora de la segunda mejor marca en lo que va de siglo (21,14 metros) en una prueba marcada como pocas por el antiguo dopaje de los países del Este. Octava ha sido la lanzadora de jabalina china Yan Ziyi, que a sus 18 años se ha situado segunda en el ranking mundial de todos los tiempos con 71.74 metros, sólo superada por la checa Barbora Spotakova. Y tras María, en décima posición, se ha situado otra lanzadora, en este caso de martillo. La canadiense Camryn Rogers, oro olímpico en París, ha afianzado su segundo puesto en la lista histórica de su especialidad con un tiro de 81,13 metros. WA ya anunció ayer los tres finalistas a mejor 'Atleta masculino del año', con el brasileño y nuevo plusmarquista mundial de 400 vallas Alison dos Santos pugnando por el galardón con el pertiguista sueco Armand Duplantis y el maratoniano keniano Sabastian Sawe, que se convirtió en Londres en el primer hombre en romper la barrera de las dos horas en un maratón homologado. Completaron el 'top ten' el británico Josh Kerr, nuevo plusmarquista mundial de la milla; el estadounidense Ja’Kobe Tharp, nuevo plusmarquista mundial de los 110 vallas; el velocista estadounidense Kenneth Bednarek, doble campeón de 100 y 200 metros en el Ultimate Championship; el cuatrocentista botsuano Collen Kebinatshipi, el lanzando de jabalina de Sri Lanka Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, el triplista italiano Andy Díaz y el lanzador de disco esloveno Kristjan Čeh.
